evidence: The fixture is ESLint's RuleTester case `/* eslint-disable rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file */`: RuleTester registers the rule under the alias rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file, and the recording, which runs the rule under its own id max-classes-per-file, reports 3:1 because ESLint matches directive names exactly. The port also honours Oxlint 1.88.0's comments (suppress.oxlint `max-classes-per-file`), and Oxlint matches a directive name with a `/` by its part after the last `/` (crates/oxc_linter/src/disable_directives.rs at oxlint_v1.88.0), so the alias silences the port here. The disagreement is the harness's alias, not the rule: without the alias neither tool's directive would apply, and with ESLint's real id both would.
